problem:
Find the inverse of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$
given that $det(A)=4.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix Using the Cofactor Method

feedback.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $24.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{13}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{31}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{31} & =(-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =24-0 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{13}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{31}=\frac{1}{24}\cdot 24=1.\end{aligned}
$$
